stem: A 'perfectly competitive market' is characterised by __________.
options: A large number of buyers and sellers, a homogeneous product, free entry and exit, and perfect knowledge
solution: A PERFECTLY COMPETITIVE MARKET is characterised by: a LARGE NUMBER of BUYERS and SELLERS (each too small to affect price); a HOMOGENEOUS (identical) PRODUCT; FREE ENTRY and EXIT of firms; and PERFECT KNOWLEDGE/information among all participants. These features make each firm a price taker. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In perfect competition, an individual firm is a 'price taker', meaning it __________.
options: Must accept the market-determined price and cannot influence it by its own actions
solution: In perfect competition, an individual firm is a PRICE TAKER — it must ACCEPT the PRICE determined by the overall MARKET (by industry demand and supply) and CANNOT INFLUENCE it by its own actions, because it is too small a part of the market. It decides only how much to produce at that given price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The demand curve facing an individual firm under perfect competition is __________.
options: A horizontal (perfectly elastic) line at the market price
solution: The demand curve facing an INDIVIDUAL FIRM under perfect competition is a HORIZONTAL (PERFECTLY ELASTIC) line at the MARKET PRICE. Since the firm can sell any quantity at that price (and nothing above it), its demand curve is a flat line — which is also its average revenue and marginal revenue curve. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Total Revenue' (TR) is calculated as __________.
options: Price multiplied by quantity sold (P × Q)
solution: TOTAL REVENUE (TR) = PRICE × QUANTITY sold (P × Q). It is the total amount of money a firm receives from selling its output. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Average Revenue' (AR) is __________.
options: Total revenue divided by quantity (TR/Q), which equals the price
solution: AVERAGE REVENUE (AR) = TOTAL REVENUE ÷ QUANTITY (TR/Q) = (P × Q)/Q = PRICE. So average revenue always EQUALS the PRICE per unit. The AR curve is therefore the firm's demand curve. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Marginal Revenue' (MR) is __________.
options: The addition to total revenue from selling one more unit (ΔTR/ΔQ)
solution: MARGINAL REVENUE (MR) is the ADDITION to TOTAL REVENUE from selling ONE MORE UNIT of output: MR = ΔTR/ΔQ. It measures the extra revenue the last unit sold contributes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Under perfect competition, the relationship between price (P), average revenue (AR), and marginal revenue (MR) is __________.
options: P = AR = MR (all equal and constant at the market price)
solution: Under PERFECT COMPETITION, since the firm sells all units at the SAME market PRICE, we have P = AR = MR — all EQUAL and CONSTANT at the market price. Selling one more unit adds exactly the price to revenue (MR = P), and the average revenue is also the price (AR = P). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The firm's profit is maximised where __________.
options: Marginal revenue equals marginal cost (MR = MC), with MC rising
Total revenue is highest regardless of cost
solution: A firm's PROFIT is MAXIMISED where MARGINAL REVENUE EQUALS MARGINAL COST (MR = MC), provided MC is RISING (cutting MR from below). If MR > MC, producing more adds to profit; if MR < MC, producing less does. Profit is greatest exactly at MR = MC (the second-order condition being that MC is rising). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Under perfect competition, since P = MR, the profit-maximising condition can be written as __________.
solution: Under PERFECT COMPETITION, because PRICE = MARGINAL REVENUE (P = MR), the profit-maximising condition MR = MC becomes P = MC. So the competitive firm produces the output at which PRICE EQUALS MARGINAL COST (with MC rising). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A firm earns 'supernormal' (positive economic) profit when, at the profit-maximising output, __________.
options: Price (AR) is greater than average total cost (P > ATC)
Price is less than average cost
solution: A firm earns SUPERNORMAL (POSITIVE economic) PROFIT when, at the profit-maximising output (P = MC), the PRICE (AR) is GREATER than the AVERAGE TOTAL COST (P > ATC). The excess of price over average cost, times quantity, is the supernormal profit. So option 1 is correct.

stem: A firm earns 'normal profit' (breaks even) when __________.
options: Price equals average total cost (P = ATC), so economic profit is zero
solution: A firm earns NORMAL PROFIT (breaks even in the economic sense) when PRICE EQUALS AVERAGE TOTAL COST (P = ATC), so ECONOMIC PROFIT is ZERO. Normal profit is the minimum return that keeps the entrepreneur in business (it is included in economic costs). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A firm incurs a 'loss' when __________.
options: Price is less than average total cost (P < ATC)
solution: A firm incurs a LOSS when, at the profit-maximising output, PRICE is LESS than AVERAGE TOTAL COST (P < ATC) — it cannot cover its full costs. Whether it continues producing in the short run then depends on whether price covers average variable cost. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the SHORT RUN, a firm will continue to produce (rather than shut down) as long as __________.
options: Price is at least equal to average variable cost (P ≥ AVC)
Price is above average total cost
solution: In the SHORT RUN, a firm will CONTINUE to PRODUCE (even at a loss) as long as PRICE is at least equal to AVERAGE VARIABLE COST (P ≥ AVC). If price covers AVC, the firm covers its variable costs and part of its fixed costs, so producing is better than shutting down (where it would lose all its fixed costs). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'shut-down point' in the short run is where __________.
options: Price equals the minimum average variable cost (P = minimum AVC)
solution: The SHUT-DOWN POINT in the short run is where PRICE equals the MINIMUM AVERAGE VARIABLE COST (P = minimum AVC). Below this price, the firm cannot even cover its variable costs, so it is better off SHUTTING DOWN (producing zero) and losing only its fixed costs. At or above it, the firm keeps producing. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The short-run supply curve of a perfectly competitive firm is __________.
options: The portion of its marginal cost (MC) curve above the minimum of average variable cost (AVC)
solution: The SHORT-RUN SUPPLY CURVE of a perfectly competitive firm is the RISING portion of its MARGINAL COST (MC) curve that lies ABOVE the MINIMUM of AVERAGE VARIABLE COST (AVC). Below minimum AVC, the firm shuts down (supplies zero); above it, the firm produces where P = MC, so the MC curve above AVC shows how much it supplies at each price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'long-run shut-down point' (where the firm exits the industry) is where __________.
options: Price equals the minimum average total cost (P = minimum ATC)
solution: In the LONG RUN, all costs are variable, so a firm will EXIT the industry if PRICE is below the MINIMUM AVERAGE TOTAL COST. The LONG-RUN shut-down/exit point is where PRICE equals the MINIMUM ATC (P = minimum ATC) — below this, the firm cannot cover its full costs and leaves. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The long-run supply curve of a perfectly competitive firm is __________.
options: The portion of its marginal cost curve above the minimum of average total cost (ATC)
solution: The LONG-RUN SUPPLY CURVE of a perfectly competitive firm is the portion of its MARGINAL COST curve that lies ABOVE the MINIMUM of AVERAGE TOTAL COST (ATC). In the long run the firm must cover ALL its costs, so it supplies only at prices at or above minimum ATC. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the LONG RUN under perfect competition, firms tend to earn only __________.
options: Normal profit (zero economic profit), because free entry and exit competes away supernormal profits and losses
solution: In the LONG RUN under perfect competition, firms tend to earn only NORMAL PROFIT (ZERO ECONOMIC PROFIT). This is because FREE ENTRY and EXIT competes away profits and losses: supernormal profits ATTRACT new firms (raising supply, lowering price) until profits vanish; losses cause firms to EXIT (reducing supply, raising price) until losses vanish. Equilibrium is at P = minimum ATC. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Free entry and exit of firms is important because it __________.
options: Ensures that in the long run, only normal profits are earned and resources are allocated efficiently
Has no effect on the market
solution: FREE ENTRY and EXIT is important because it ENSURES that in the LONG RUN only NORMAL PROFITS are earned (economic profit is competed away) and RESOURCES are ALLOCATED EFFICIENTLY — firms enter where profits exist and leave where losses occur, driving the industry to an efficient equilibrium at minimum average cost. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'market supply curve' in a perfectly competitive market is obtained by __________.
options: Horizontally summing the individual supply curves of all firms in the market
solution: The MARKET (industry) SUPPLY CURVE in perfect competition is obtained by HORIZONTALLY SUMMING (adding the quantities supplied by) the INDIVIDUAL SUPPLY CURVES of ALL FIRMS at each price. It shows the total quantity all firms together supply at each price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'Law of Supply' states that, other things equal, __________.
options: As the price of a good rises, the quantity supplied rises (a direct/positive relationship)
Price and quantity supplied move inversely
solution: The LAW of SUPPLY states that, OTHER THINGS EQUAL, as the PRICE of a good RISES, the QUANTITY SUPPLIED RISES (and as price falls, quantity supplied falls). There is a DIRECT (POSITIVE) relationship between price and quantity supplied, giving the supply curve its upward slope. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The supply curve slopes upward because __________.
options: Higher prices make it profitable to produce more, and rising marginal costs mean firms need higher prices to supply more
solution: The SUPPLY CURVE slopes UPWARD because HIGHER PRICES make it PROFITABLE to PRODUCE MORE, and because MARGINAL COSTS RISE as output increases (law of diminishing returns) — so firms need HIGHER PRICES to justify supplying larger quantities (since they produce where P = MC). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A movement ALONG the supply curve (change in quantity supplied) is caused by __________.
options: A change in the price of the good itself
A change in the number of firms
solution: A MOVEMENT ALONG the supply curve — a CHANGE in QUANTITY SUPPLIED — is caused ONLY by a change in the PRICE of the GOOD ITSELF (other factors constant). Changes in technology, input prices, or the number of firms instead SHIFT the whole supply curve (change in supply). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A SHIFT of the supply curve (change in supply) is caused by __________.
options: Factors other than the good's own price — such as input prices, technology, taxes/subsidies, and the number of firms
solution: A SHIFT of the supply curve — a CHANGE in SUPPLY — is caused by factors OTHER than the good's OWN PRICE: INPUT (factor) PRICES, TECHNOLOGY, TAXES and SUBSIDIES, PRICES of RELATED GOODS, the NUMBER of FIRMS, and expectations. A rightward shift means more supply at every price; a leftward shift means less. So option 1 is correct.

stem: An improvement in technology will, other things equal, cause the supply curve to __________.
options: Shift rightward (increase supply, as production becomes cheaper/more efficient)
solution: An IMPROVEMENT in TECHNOLOGY makes production CHEAPER and MORE EFFICIENT (lowering costs), so firms are willing to supply MORE at every price — the supply curve SHIFTS RIGHTWARD (increase in supply). So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Price elasticity of supply' measures __________.
options: The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in the good's price
The total supply of a good
The slope of the demand curve
solution: PRICE ELASTICITY of SUPPLY measures the RESPONSIVENESS of the QUANTITY SUPPLIED to a CHANGE in the good's PRICE — calculated as the percentage change in quantity supplied divided by the percentage change in price. It shows how sensitive producers are to price changes. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Market equilibrium in a competitive market occurs where __________.
options: The quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied (demand curve intersects supply curve)
solution: MARKET EQUILIBRIUM occurs where the QUANTITY DEMANDED EQUALS the QUANTITY SUPPLIED — where the DEMAND curve INTERSECTS the SUPPLY curve. This determines the EQUILIBRIUM PRICE and EQUILIBRIUM QUANTITY, at which there is no tendency for price to change. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The average revenue (AR) curve of a perfectly competitive firm coincides with __________.
options: Its demand curve (both are the horizontal line at the market price)
solution: The AVERAGE REVENUE (AR) curve of a perfectly competitive firm COINCIDES with its DEMAND CURVE — both are the SAME HORIZONTAL LINE at the market PRICE (since AR = P, and the firm can sell any quantity at that price). The MR curve coincides with it too (MR = AR = P). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Under perfect competition, the total revenue (TR) curve is __________.
options: An upward-sloping straight line from the origin (since TR = P × Q and P is constant)
solution: Under PERFECT COMPETITION, the TOTAL REVENUE (TR) curve is an UPWARD-SLOPING STRAIGHT LINE from the ORIGIN, because TR = PRICE × QUANTITY and the PRICE is CONSTANT — so TR rises in direct proportion to quantity sold, with a constant slope equal to the price. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): A perfectly competitive firm produces where P = MC. Reason (R): Since P = MR for such a firm, the profit-maximising condition MR = MC reduces to P = MC. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — a perfectly competitive firm produces where P = MC. R is TRUE and correctly EXPLAINS A: because for such a firm PRICE = MARGINAL REVENUE (P = MR), the general profit-maximising condition MR = MC REDUCES to P = MC. So R is the correct explanation of A. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why might a firm continue to produce in the short run despite making a loss?
options: If price covers average variable cost, producing minimises the loss compared to shutting down (which would lose all fixed costs)
Because it can ignore all costs
Because fixed costs disappear when it produces
solution: A firm might CONTINUE to PRODUCE at a LOSS in the SHORT RUN if the PRICE COVERS AVERAGE VARIABLE COST (P ≥ AVC). By producing, it recovers all its variable costs and CONTRIBUTES something toward its FIXED COSTS, so its loss is SMALLER than if it SHUT DOWN (where it would lose the entire fixed cost). Producing thus minimises the loss. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the long-run equilibrium of a perfectly competitive industry, price equals __________.
options: The minimum long-run average cost (P = minimum LRAC), so firms are productively efficient
solution: In LONG-RUN EQUILIBRIUM of a perfectly competitive industry, PRICE equals the MINIMUM LONG-RUN AVERAGE COST (P = minimum LRAC). Free entry and exit drive profits to zero (P = ATC), and the firm produces at the lowest point of its LRAC — so it is PRODUCTIVELY EFFICIENT (producing at least-cost). Also P = MC gives allocative efficiency. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The condition P = MC in competitive equilibrium is significant because it implies __________.
options: Allocative efficiency — the value consumers place on the last unit (price) equals its cost of production (MC)
That the firm makes maximum profit forever
solution: The condition P = MC in competitive equilibrium is significant because it implies ALLOCATIVE EFFICIENCY: the PRICE (the VALUE consumers place on the LAST UNIT) EQUALS the MARGINAL COST (the cost of producing that last unit). Resources are allocated so that the benefit of the last unit just equals its cost — society's welfare is maximised. So option 1 is correct.

stem: If the market price rises above a competitive firm's average total cost, in the short run the firm __________.
options: Earns supernormal profit, which in the long run attracts new firms into the industry
solution: If the market PRICE RISES ABOVE a firm's ATC, in the SHORT RUN the firm earns SUPERNORMAL (positive economic) PROFIT. In the LONG RUN, this profit ATTRACTS NEW FIRMS into the industry (free entry), increasing supply and pushing the price back down until only normal profit remains. So option 1 is correct.

stem: If firms in a competitive industry are making losses, in the long run __________.
options: Some firms exit the industry, reducing supply and raising the price until remaining firms earn normal profit
solution: If firms are making LOSSES, in the LONG RUN some firms EXIT the industry (free exit). This REDUCES market SUPPLY, which RAISES the PRICE, until the losses are eliminated and the REMAINING firms earn NORMAL PROFIT (P = minimum ATC). So option 1 is correct.

stem: A homogeneous product (identical across sellers) is important for perfect competition because it __________.
options: Ensures buyers have no reason to prefer one seller's product over another, so all must charge the same single price
Allows sellers to charge different prices
solution: A HOMOGENEOUS (identical) PRODUCT is important because it ensures BUYERS have NO REASON to PREFER one seller's product over another's. With identical goods and perfect knowledge, no seller can charge more than others (buyers would switch), so ALL sellers must charge the SAME single market PRICE — reinforcing price-taking behaviour. So option 1 is correct.

stem: 'Perfect knowledge' (perfect information) in a competitive market means that __________.
options: All buyers and sellers are fully aware of prices and products throughout the market
solution: PERFECT KNOWLEDGE (perfect information) means that ALL BUYERS and SELLERS are FULLY AWARE of the PRICES and PRODUCTS prevailing THROUGHOUT the market. This ensures a single uniform price (no one pays more or accepts less than the going price) and prevents any seller from exploiting ignorance. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Total profit of a firm is calculated as __________.
options: Total revenue minus total cost (TR − TC)
solution: TOTAL PROFIT = TOTAL REVENUE − TOTAL COST (TR − TC). It is maximised at the output where the gap between TR and TC is greatest — which corresponds to the point where MR = MC. So option 1 is correct.

stem: At the profit-maximising output, per-unit profit equals __________.
options: Price minus average total cost (P − ATC), and total profit is this times quantity
solution: At the profit-maximising output, PER-UNIT PROFIT = PRICE − AVERAGE TOTAL COST (P − ATC), and TOTAL PROFIT = (P − ATC) × QUANTITY. If P > ATC there is supernormal profit; if P = ATC, normal profit; if P < ATC, a loss. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Why is MR = MC alone not sufficient for profit maximisation (why must MC also be rising)?
options: Because MR = MC could also occur where MC is falling (a loss-minimising/profit-minimising point); profit is maximised only where MC cuts MR from below
solution: MR = MC alone is NOT sufficient because this equality can occur at TWO points — one where MC is FALLING (which is actually a point of minimum profit/maximum loss) and one where MC is RISING. Profit is MAXIMISED only at the output where MC = MR AND MC is RISING (cutting MR from below). This is the second-order condition. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of perfect competition?
options: A large number of buyers and sellers
solution: Producing DIFFERENTIATED (BRANDED) PRODUCTS is NOT a feature of perfect competition — perfect competition requires a HOMOGENEOUS (identical) product. Product differentiation is a feature of MONOPOLISTIC COMPETITION. The large number of buyers/sellers, free entry and exit, and perfect knowledge ARE features of perfect competition. So option 1 is correct.

stem: When market demand for a good increases (demand curve shifts right), the short-run effect on a competitive market is __________.
options: A rise in the equilibrium price and quantity
A fall in both price and quantity
solution: When MARKET DEMAND INCREASES (demand curve shifts RIGHT), with supply unchanged, the equilibrium moves up along the supply curve: both the EQUILIBRIUM PRICE and the EQUILIBRIUM QUANTITY RISE. (Higher demand pushes price up, and the higher price induces firms to supply more.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: When market supply increases (supply curve shifts right) with demand unchanged, the effect is __________.
options: A fall in the equilibrium price and a rise in the equilibrium quantity
A rise in both price and quantity
A rise in price, fall in quantity
solution: When MARKET SUPPLY INCREASES (supply curve shifts RIGHT) with demand unchanged, the equilibrium moves down along the demand curve: the EQUILIBRIUM PRICE FALLS and the EQUILIBRIUM QUANTITY RISES. (More supply lowers the price, and the lower price raises quantity demanded.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: A perfectly elastic supply curve (elasticity = infinity) is __________.
options: A horizontal line, where any quantity is supplied at a given price
solution: A PERFECTLY ELASTIC supply curve (elasticity of supply = infinity) is a HORIZONTAL line — at the given price, producers are willing to supply ANY QUANTITY, but they would supply nothing at a lower price. (A perfectly inelastic supply, by contrast, is vertical.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: A perfectly inelastic supply curve (elasticity = 0) is __________.
options: A vertical line, where the quantity supplied is fixed regardless of price
solution: A PERFECTLY INELASTIC supply curve (elasticity of supply = 0) is a VERTICAL line — the QUANTITY supplied is FIXED regardless of the PRICE (e.g., the supply of a fixed stock of a perishable good in a short period, or land). Quantity does not respond to price at all. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The reason a competitive firm's marginal revenue is constant (equal to price) is that __________.
options: It can sell any additional unit at the same market price without lowering the price
It must cut price to sell more
It faces a downward-sloping demand curve
solution: A competitive firm's MARGINAL REVENUE is CONSTANT (equal to PRICE) because, being a price taker, it can SELL any ADDITIONAL UNIT at the SAME market PRICE WITHOUT LOWERING the price. So each extra unit adds exactly the price to revenue (MR = P). (A monopolist, by contrast, must cut price to sell more, so its MR falls below price.) So option 1 is correct.

stem: The competitive market outcome (P = MC) is often regarded as the benchmark of efficiency because __________.
options: Resources are allocated to their most valued uses, and goods are produced at the lowest possible cost in the long run
solution: The competitive outcome (P = MC) is regarded as the BENCHMARK of EFFICIENCY because RESOURCES are ALLOCATED to their MOST VALUED USES (allocative efficiency, since price = marginal cost), and in the long run goods are PRODUCED at the LOWEST POSSIBLE COST (productive efficiency, since P = minimum ATC). This maximises social welfare, which is why perfect competition is used as an ideal standard. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a revenue concept for a competitive firm?
options: AR = price = demand curve; MR = price = constant; TR = price × quantity (a straight line from origin)
AR falls with output; MR is negative; TR is U-shaped
AR = total cost; MR = fixed cost; TR = zero
All revenue concepts are equal to marginal cost
solution: For a COMPETITIVE FIRM, the correct matches are: AVERAGE REVENUE (AR) = PRICE = the DEMAND CURVE (horizontal line); MARGINAL REVENUE (MR) = PRICE = CONSTANT; and TOTAL REVENUE (TR) = PRICE × QUANTITY, a STRAIGHT LINE from the ORIGIN. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 'break-even point' for a firm is the output level at which __________.
options: Total revenue equals total cost, so the firm earns exactly normal profit (zero economic profit)
Total revenue is at its maximum
solution: The BREAK-EVEN POINT is the output level at which TOTAL REVENUE EQUALS TOTAL COST (TR = TC), so the firm earns exactly NORMAL PROFIT (ZERO economic profit) — neither supernormal profit nor loss. At this point, price equals average total cost (P = ATC). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'The Theory of the Firm under Perfect Competition' is that:
options: Firms can set any price they wish

In PERFECT COMPETITION — marked by MANY buyers and sellers, a HOMOGENEOUS product, FREE ENTRY and EXIT, and PERFECT KNOWLEDGE — each firm is a PRICE TAKER facing a horizontal demand curve, so PRICE = AR = MR; the firm MAXIMISES PROFIT where MR = MC (i.e., P = MC with MC rising), earning supernormal profit, normal profit, or a loss depending on how price compares with average cost; in the SHORT RUN it produces as long as price covers average VARIABLE cost (the MC curve above minimum AVC is its supply curve), while FREE ENTRY and EXIT drive the LONG RUN to NORMAL PROFIT (P = minimum ATC); this yields allocative and productive EFFICIENCY, making perfect competition the benchmark ideal market
Profit is maximised where price is highest
solution: The chapter's overall message is that in PERFECT COMPETITION — characterised by a LARGE NUMBER of BUYERS and SELLERS, a HOMOGENEOUS (identical) PRODUCT, FREE ENTRY and EXIT of firms, and PERFECT KNOWLEDGE — each firm is a PRICE TAKER facing a HORIZONTAL (perfectly elastic) demand curve, so PRICE = AVERAGE REVENUE = MARGINAL REVENUE. The firm MAXIMISES PROFIT where MARGINAL REVENUE EQUALS MARGINAL COST (MR = MC), which reduces to P = MC (with MC rising). Depending on how PRICE compares with AVERAGE COST, the firm earns SUPERNORMAL PROFIT (P > ATC), NORMAL PROFIT (P = ATC), or a LOSS (P < ATC). In the SHORT RUN, the firm continues producing as long as PRICE covers AVERAGE VARIABLE COST — so the portion of its MC curve above minimum AVC is its SUPPLY CURVE — while in the LONG RUN, FREE ENTRY and EXIT compete away profits and losses, driving the industry to NORMAL PROFIT at P = MINIMUM ATC. This outcome achieves both ALLOCATIVE EFFICIENCY (P = MC) and PRODUCTIVE EFFICIENCY (least-cost production), making perfect competition the BENCHMARK IDEAL market. So the overall message is option 2.
